user.title: Läutwerk
user.description: Set up Läutwerk? Rules are created afterwards in the Läutwerk card on a dashboard.

init.title: Household quiet time
init.description: Signals without their own quiet time follow this one. Leave both times empty for none.

data_description.mode: Skip them, or send them when the quiet time ends.

acknowledge.name: Acknowledge
acknowledge.description: Marks reminders as done. With 'rule': the open reminders of that rule (or its next planned reminder, as far as the early setting of the rule allows it). Without 'rule': all open reminders of all rules. Returns acknowledged (reminder ids) and too_early (text such as the next due date when it was too early, else null) when response data is requested.

rule.name: Rule
rule.description: Rule id (see get_rules). Empty: all open reminders.

reminder_id.name: Reminder
reminder_id.description: Acknowledge exactly this reminder (id from get_rules → status.reminders).

person.name: Person
person.description: Name stored as 'acknowledged by'. Default: the person of the calling user.

snooze.name: Snooze
snooze.description: Reminds again later: open reminders become planned again and remind once more when the duration is over or at the given time (unless they expire first). Give either 'duration' or 'until'. Without 'rule': all open reminders.

rule.name: Rule
rule.description: Rule id. Empty: all open reminders.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: Minutes, or a duration such as 30m, 3h, 1d.

until.name: Until
until.description: Time of day, e.g. 07:00 (the next time it is reached).

reopen.name: Reopen
reopen.description: Undoes the acknowledgement of a reminder (e.g. a mis-tap) as long as it has not expired: it is open again (reminded or planned). Signals are not sent again; actions run when done are not undone.

reminder_id.name: Reminder
reminder_id.description: Id of the acknowledged reminder (get_rules → status.reminders).

trigger.name: Trigger
trigger.description: Reminds now: sends the immediate signals of the rule for its open or next planned reminder, regardless of the reminder times.

start.name: Start
start.description: Starts a reminder of a rule that is driven by start_triggers, exactly as if a trigger had fired: nothing happens while a reminder of the rule is open. Fails for rules without start_triggers.

test_signal.name: Test signal
test_signal.description: Sends one signal of a rule right now, ignoring its conditions, quiet times and limits. Uses the open reminder, else the next matching event, else a sample event for tomorrow. Give either 'signal' (id of a saved signal) or 'config' (a signal object that is not saved, requires admin).

signal.name: Signal
signal.description: Id of a signal of the rule.

config.name: Signal object
config.description: Unsaved signal to try out (same fields as a signal in create_rule).

get_rules.name: Get rules
get_rules.description: Returns the rules (configuration as used by create_rule/update_rule) with their runtime status: state (planned/reminded/done/missed/inactive), reminders with variables, next matching event, calendar errors.

rule.name: Rule
rule.description: One or more rule ids. Empty: all rules.

create_rule.name: Create rule
create_rule.description: Creates a rule and returns its id. Requires admin.

config.name: Rule
config.description: Rule object. Required: name, reminders (list of objects with 'at'; not needed for start_triggers rules) and exactly one source: sources (entity ids: calendar.*, todo.* lists with due dates, date.*, datetime.*, input_datetime.*, timestamp/date sensor.*) or interval. Optional: id, icon, color, headline and headline_plural (editable card headline with variables in curly braces, plural variant used for several hits), enabled, filter (all_day, keywords with columns = list of variable names and rows = list of objects with match, mode contains/startswith/regex, optional own color (#rrggbb) and icon (e.g. mdi:recycle) and one value per column), signals (list). Every signal: id, type, enabled, when ('now' = at the reminder time, or an object with opportunity = Home Assistant trigger(s) as in automations and manual_only = only real operation, not automations; an opportunity signal fires whenever the trigger fires while the reminder is open), conditions (Home Assistant conditions, 'only if') with conditions_match all/any, limit (per_reminder = maximum sends per reminder, min_interval = minutes between sends), quiet (list of objects with from, to as HH:MM and mode skip or defer = send when the quiet time ends). type notify: targets = list of notify.xxx actions and/or audience all/present/persons/assignee (with persons = list of person entities; uses their mobile app devices), title, title_plural, title_repeat, message_repeat (texts from the second reminder on), message, message_plural, actions = push buttons, list of objects with label and either ack: true or snooze: duration such as 3h, data. type light_signal: entities = light entities, pattern (effect blink/pulse, count, interval in seconds), color (name, #hex or r,g,b) or color_from = keyword column holding the colour, brightness in percent, restore (bring the light back to its previous state, default true). type announce: players = media players, text, text_plural, text_repeat (text from the second reminder on), volume 0-100, tts = TTS entity, language, voice. type action: actions = any Home Assistant action sequence; the text variables are available as template variables. acknowledge (further ways to acknowledge, list of objects: type tag with tag_id = NFC tag; type trigger with trigger = Home Assistant trigger such as a door contact, zone or button), repeat ('none' or an object with every = minutes or a duration such as 1h, and max = number of repetitions), interval (every = days such as 90 or '12w', start = first due date: due again that many days after the last acknowledgement; overdue = reminds daily), activation (conditions, match all/any, season with from/to as MM-DD: the rule is only active then), on_done (Home Assistant actions run when acknowledged, variables plus person and via), on_missed and on_reminded (actions run when a reminder becomes missed / after every reminder incl. repeats and stages, variables plus rule_id, reminder_id, nr, seit_min), assignee (persons = person entities, rotation fixed/weekly/per_event/after_last, substitute = person that takes over at the first reminder if substitute_when (entity_id and state) holds; text variable zustaendig, push audience 'assignee'), escalation (list of stages with after = duration such as 2h or time of day such as 21:30, counted from the first reminder, and optional min_age = duration; the stage is skipped if it is closer than that to the first reminder, and optional color = #rrggbb shown in the card; a signal with stage n starts with that stage; every_stage: true sends a signal at the first reminder and at every stage; a time of day means the next such time after the first reminder), start_triggers (list of Home Assistant triggers as in automations; instead of calendars the rule starts a reminder whenever one fires and none is open; reminders and filter are ignored, expire defaults to '+12h' and must not be event_start/event_end; start it by hand with the start action), early (object with mode off, hours or always, default hours with hours 1-720, default 24: when a planned reminder may be acknowledged before its time; ignored by trigger rules), early_feedback (object with message and clear_after seconds 0-3600, default 10, or null: short push after a too early attempt to the person, else the assignee; variables of the next planned reminder), confirm (object with message and clear_after seconds 0-3600, default 10: confirmation push to whoever acknowledged, else the assignee), expire also accepts a plus sign and a duration such as '+12h' (after the start), lookahead_days (1-365, default 14, days the calendars are read ahead, must exceed the earliest reminder offset), visible (default true; false hides the rule in the card overview), ack_label, bundle (events of the same day become one reminder, default true), expire (default event_end). Times: '-1d 17:00' (day before at 17:00), '09:00' (event day), '-2h' (before the start), 'event_day 12:00', 'event_end'. Text variables, written in curly braces in the texts: titel, rest, beschreibung, ort, kalender, wann, datum, uhrzeit, seit (e.g. for 25 minutes), seit_min, erinnert_um, nr (number of the reminder), one per keyword column and its plural with an appended n (e.g. tonne / tonnen).

update_rule.name: Update rule
update_rule.description: Changes a rule: the given top-level keys replace the stored ones (e.g. only 'signals' or 'reminders'); open reminders are kept. Requires admin.

delete_rule.name: Delete rule
delete_rule.description: Deletes a rule with its reminders and entities. Requires admin.

duplicate_rule.name: Duplicate rule
duplicate_rule.description: Copies a rule; the copy is switched off. Returns the new id. Requires admin.

new_rule.name: New id
new_rule.description: Id of the copy (default: derived from the name).

export_rules.name: Export rules
export_rules.description: Returns rules as YAML (one rule as a mapping, several as a list) – for backups or to copy them to another Home Assistant.

rule.name: Rule
rule.description: One or more rule ids. Empty: all rules.

import_rules.name: Import rules
import_rules.description: Creates rules from YAML as returned by export_rules. Ids that exist already get a new one. All rules are checked first; if one is invalid, none is created. Requires admin.

yaml.name: YAML
yaml.description: One rule (mapping) or a list of rules.

rule.name: Rule
rule.description: One or more rule ids. Empty: all rules.

disable.name: Disable
disable.description: Switches rules off; their open reminders are dropped.

rule.name: Rule
rule.description: One or more rule ids. Empty: all rules.

no_upcoming_event.message: Rule {rule} has no upcoming event to remind of.

signal_failed.message: The signal could not be sent – see the log for details.

cannot_reopen.message: Reminder {reminder} cannot be reopened (not acknowledged or already expired).

missing_entities.title: Läutwerk rule "{rule}" refers to missing entities
missing_entities.description:
The rule "{rule}" uses entities or actions that do not exist (any more): {entities}.

Calendars that are missing are not read, signals to missing lights, speakers or phones are not sent. Restore them or edit the rule in the Läutwerk card. This message disappears as soon as everything is available again.
